habit_scope: Final grade, drive, walks, eavestroughs after the 2-story house is up. NOT P01 site prep. CMHC Ch28 + Ch25 + Ch2 Landscaping. Decks Ch26 not this first pass unless site.
how_it_is_done: CMHC Ch2 Landscaping: finished grading, driveways, steps, walkways, ground cover, shrubs and trees. Deck framing usually while landscaping — Ch26 decks are NOT this first pass. About one week; delayed until warm weather if the house finishes in fall/winter. Not a lag-day invention — a weather hold named by the book. This is not P01 site prep.

Ch28: slope all surfaces away from foundation walls at least 5 percent; 10 percent for the first 2 m (6 ft 6 in) to stay positive after backfill settles. Impermeable surfaces next to the house (driveways) ≥2 percent. Swale where a reverse slope meets the house drainage (Fig 3). Direct roof and driveway water away from the house — not into the foundation drain (Ch2 printed 13). AF&PA (US): grade to drain away. Ch29: first-year settlement may pond — restore slope. Canadian slopes — confirm AHJ.

Driveway ≥2.4 m (8 ft); 3 m (10 ft) if it is also the walk. Suggested max gradient 5 percent, cross slope 2 percent. Compacted uniform surface; gravel/crushed stone ≥100 mm (4 in) after compaction. Asphalt ≥40 mm (1-1/2 in); concrete ≥100 mm (4 in). Concrete control joints 3–3.5 m (10–12 ft); 6–12 mm (1/4–1/2 in) pre-moulded filler isolating from curbs, garage floor, and foundation wall. Placing/finishing/curing as Ch7. HUD §4.6 (US): nominal 4 in (ACI 302) for drives/garages/sidewalks. Keep both thickness stories. CMHC Ch3 32 MPa (4,600 psi) air-entrained for drives — Canadian, confirm AHJ.

Walks: concrete / pavers / flagstone on a compacted base; max 5 percent along, 2 percent cross. Concrete walks ≥100 mm (4 in); control joints about 1.5× walk width. Pavers/flagstones on compacted sand or stone dust.

Ch25 eavestroughs: not required by NBC but recommended. Install AFTER exterior finish is complete. On the fascia, close to the shingle overhang, slight slope to downspouts. Metal brackets inside the trough; corrosion-resistant spikes 150 mm (6 in) long about 750 mm (30 in) apart with a spacer tube, through the trough into the fascia. Downspouts: ≥two hooks/straps per 3 m (10 ft). If not to a storm sewer: elbow + extension or splash block, away from the foundation. Ice-damming note points at Fig 100 — that ice detail is P09, not a Fontana snow pack. No Ch25 gutter figure this pass — OC is text.
tools_equipment: Named: gutter spikes/brackets; splash block. Not a SKU list.
inspection_hold_points: Positive slope away from the foundation: 5 percent general, 10 percent first 6 ft 6 in (Ch28).
Drive/walk base 4 in compacted gravel; concrete 4 in; asphalt 1-1/2 in (Ch28).
Isolation joint at garage slab and foundation (Ch28).
Do not dump roof water into the foundation drain (Ch2).
typical_duration_sfr: CMHC Ch2: about one week for landscaping — Canadian sample; delayed to warm weather if winter finish. No lag days invented.
when_this_beats_habit: This is the habit. Decks are Ch26, not this first pass.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Mixing this with P01 site prep. Draining roofs into the footing drain. Skipping the 10 percent near the wall after backfill settles.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They pour a drive. What they skip is 10 percent in the first 6 feet and gutters after siding, not before.
permit_gate_notes: CMHC Canadian slopes. Confirm AHJ. Isolation joints at the house.
risk_if_swapped_late: Regrading after landscaping is a tear-up. Catch the 10 percent while the dirt is still loose.
plain_language_summary: This is not site prep. Dirt slopes away — 10 percent in the first six feet. Four inches of rock, then four inches of concrete or an inch and a half of asphalt. Gutters after the siding, spikes every 30 inches, water onto a splash block, not into the footing drain.
spanish_summary: Esto no es P01. El terreno cae lejos — 10 por ciento en los primeros seis pies. Cuatro pulgadas de piedra, luego concreto de 4 o asfalto de 1-1/2. Canalones despues del siding, clavos cada 30 pulgadas, agua a un splash block, no al drain del cimiento.
